related_questions.question: What helps you recover from COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: For mild or normal cases of COVID-19, rest, over-the-counter medications for symptoms, and monitoring your health are key to recovery. If you have a fever or body aches, acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help. It's also important to isolate from others, wear a mask when around a caregiver, and monitor your health for any worsening symptoms.

list.title: Over-the-counter medications:

list.title: Isolate:
list.snippet: Stay away from others to prevent spread. If you need care, choose a healthy caregiver who is not at high risk for severe disease.

list.title: Masking:
list.snippet: If you need to be around others, wear a mask to minimize the spread of infectious particles.

list.title: Monitor symptoms:
list.snippet: Watch for any worsening symptoms and seek immediate medical attention for any emergencies, says UnityPoint Health.

related_questions.question: What is the recovery time for COVID-19?

text_blocks.snippet: The typical recovery time from COVID-19 can vary, but most people recover within a couple of weeks. Mild cases may resolve within a week or two, while more severe cases could take up to six weeks. Studies show that symptoms like fatigue, headaches, and breathing difficulties can linger even after the initial infection is over. The CDC recommends isolation until symptoms improve and you've been fever-free for 24 hours without medication, and at least five days have passed since symptoms started. The WHO states that for a condition known as "long COVID", some individuals may experience symptoms for 4-9 months, or even longer, according to the WHO.
snippet_highlighted_words: most people recover within a couple of weeks
